text:
lucy: hi team, morning! first-day setup snag: postgres container crashes on init with `initdb: could not change permissions of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Permission denied`. i'm on an M2 mac. my compose has a bind mount `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data:delegated` because i thought delegated would be faster. any ideas?

dan: welcome lucy :wave: delegated can help perf but doesn't fix permission differences. for Postgres on mac i'd recommend a named volume instead of host bind.

kelsey: hey! +1 for named volume. if you really need host files, try the chown-in-container trick: `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/pgdata":/data alpine sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /data"` then `chmod 700 pgdata`. Postgres enforces strict perms.

lucy: hmm i tried `sudo chown` on host but docker still failed. why is chown in container different?

kelsey: on mac, Docker Desktop mediates mounts; chown from a root container applies inside the mount namespace in a way the host chown sometimes doesn't. also check you didn't force `platform: linux/amd64` in your compose (emulation can cause weird fs behavior).

dan: another quick check: some folks set `PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata` in compose to avoid initdb path expectations. Also avoid using `:delegated` for db dirs; try without the flag or switch to a named volume.

lucy: okay i'll try switching to a named volume. any gotchas with leftover volumes when switching?

kelsey: run `docker-compose down -v` to remove anonymous/previous volumes, then `docker-compose up`. If you have stale mounts, Postgres may try to reuse an incompatible state.

lucy: small follow-up: i saw an error about "permission denied" even with named volume once. turned out Docker Desktop's new gRPC FUSE caused weird mapping. disabling gRPC FUSE in Docker prefs fixed it.

dan: nice find. for reference: if you need host-level access to DB files for tooling, consider using named volume + periodic `pg_dump` to host path instead of bind mounting the DB dir. safer and avoids permission edgecases.

infra-bot: onboarding tip: recommended local setup on mac uses named volumes for Postgres, `PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata`, and `docker-compose down -v` between mount changes. See https://intranet.redwood.dev/dev-setup#local-db for details.

lucy: switched to named volume, ran `docker-compose down -v`, and postgres came up and migrations ran. thanks everyone! :tada:
